answer.why_different: The generated document appears to have moved callback-related definitions into the Path Item for `/{className}={id}`. This is both a different address and an invalid structure: callback expressions belong inside a Callback Object, while this location accepts Path Item operations, parameters, and extensions only.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP evidence defines `{notificationTarget}` as a separate resource URI and specifies that its POST request body may contain a `NotifyMOIDeletion` notification. It does not place a `notifyMOIDeletion` operation or a callback expression under the `/{className}={id}` resource.
answer.openapi: The OpenAPI reference states that a Path Item describes operations on one path, while callback expressions are patterned fields of a Callback Object. Therefore neither `notifyMOIDeletion` nor `$request.body#/notificationTarget` is valid directly under this Path Item; the generated side is explicitly not valid OpenAPI 3.0.
answer.clearer_why: The official version exposes only the valid operations and parameters for this resource. The generated version adds invalid, misleading keys at the Path Item level and duplicates callback-related content.

NotifyMOIDeletion | Type for a notifyMOIDeletion notification

differences.reason: This is an extra key at the Path Item level, where only HTTP operation keys, parameters, and specification extensions are allowed. The callback-related notification is defined by the specification as a request body type on the separate `{notificationTarget}` resource, not as a `notifyMOIDeletion` Path Item operation; the generated side is also explicitly invalid OpenAPI 3.0. Evidence: C2, O1, S11, S13.

Although `$request.body#/notificationTarget` is a valid-looking callback runtime expression, it is placed directly under this Path Item rather than inside a Callback Object. OpenAPI permits such expressions as Callback Object patterned fields, not as arbitrary fields of a Path Item; this placement therefore makes the generated document invalid. evidence.text: description: A list of pets. content: application/json: schema: type: array items: $ref: '#/components/schemas/pet' ``` #### Path Item Object Describes the operations available on a single path. A Path Item MAY be empty, due to [ACL constraints](#security-filtering). The path itself is still exposed to the documentation viewer but they will not know which operations and parameters are available. ##### Fixed Fields Field Name | Type | Description ---|:---:|--- $ref | `string` | Allows for an external definition of this path item. The referenced structure MUST be in the format of a [Path Item Object](#path-item-object). If there are conflicts between the referenced definition and this Path Item's definition, the behavior is *undefined*. summary| `string` | An optional, string summary, intended to apply to all operations in this path.

2. The [Path Item Object](#path-item-object) MAY be empty. In this case, the viewer will be aware that the path exists, but will not be able to see any of its operations or parameters. This is different than hiding the path itself from the [Paths Object](#paths-object), so the user will not be aware of its existence. This allows the documentation provider to finely control what the viewer can see.
